newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA DROP KIRSTEN FOR ONE-DAY SERIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA DROP KIRSTEN FOR ONE-DAY SERIES.

text.p: South Africa have dropped leading one-day run scorer Gary Kirsten from their squad for the forthcoming seven-match limited overs series against Australia.
Kirsten paid the price for a miserable test series, won 2-1 by Australia, in which he scored just 82 runs from six innings.
Also left out from the team which won the third test by eight wickets on Monday were all-rounder Brian McMillan, who has a heel injury and cannot bowl, and fast bowler Brett Schultz.

Kirsten set a world record for one-day internationals in a calendar year by scoring 1,442 runs, including six centuries, from 29 innings in 1996, although it was subsequently surpassed by Sachin Tendulkar who made 1,611 runs from 32 innings.
Kirsten is also second on South Africa's all time aggregate list with 2,723 runs at a record average of 46.94 from 66 matches.
Winning a first international call in the 14-man squad is 29-year-old Eastern province batsman Louis Koen, leading run scorer in domestic cricket in the last two seasons.
Recalled are Natal trio of off-spinner Derek Crookes, batsman Jonty Rhodes and all-rounder Shaun Pollock as well as Northern Transvaal fast bowler Rudi Bryson.

Squad: Hansie Cronje (captain), Adam Bacher, Daryll Cullinan, Jacques Kallis, Dave Richardson, Lance Klusener, Shaun Pollock, Pat Symcox, Louis Koen, Herschelle Gibbs, Derek Crookes, Jonty Rhodes, Allan Donald, Rudi Bryson.
